# Egap.Documents: guide for coding agents

Egap.Documents is one editable document model for Word-style flow documents: DOCX, DOC (read), RTF, OpenDocument Text,
plain text, Docling JSON and PDF, with HTML, MHTML, EPUB and Markdown from the add-on packages. It edits documents, lays
them out into pages drawn on any Egami canvas, exports PDF (tagged, PDF/A), turns PDF pages back into documents, compares
versions, fills mail merges and builds reports from code.

Namespaces: `Egap.Documents` (the model and formats), `Egap.Documents.Pdf` (`SaveAsPdf`, `PdfConvert`, `PdfToDocument`),
`Egap.Documents.Layout` (`Layout`, `LayoutOptions`), `Egap.Documents.Comparing`, `Egap.Documents.Reports` and
`Egap.Documents.Charts`.

## Egap's vocabulary

Egap has its own names. Use them, not names from other PDF, Word or Excel libraries: there is no `PdfReader`, `PdfWriter`,
`XWPFDocument`, `Range.Text` or `IWorkbook` in Egap.

- `PdfDocument` (namespace `Egap.Pdf`) is a PDF file: `PdfDocument.Open`, `PdfDocument.Create`, `PdfDocument.Merge`, then
  `Pages`, `Metadata`, `Outline`, `Form`, `Attachments`, `Signatures` and `Save`. It is `IDisposable` and keeps its file open
  until disposed.
- `Document` (namespace `Egap.Documents`) is a flow document: one model for DOCX, DOC, RTF, ODT, plain text, PDF, HTML,
  MHTML, EPUB and Markdown. `Document.Load` and `Save` pick the format; `DocumentBuilder` edits at a cursor. It is not
  disposable.
- `Workbook` and `Worksheet` (namespace `Egap.Spreadsheets`) are an Excel workbook and its sheets; `sheet["B2"]` is a
  `Cell`, `sheet.Range("A1:C9")` a `CellRange`, and `CellValue` a cell's value.
- Each format has its own class (`DocxFormat`, `RtfFormat`, `OdtFormat`, `TextFormat`, `HtmlFormat`, `EpubFormat`,
  `MarkdownFormat`) and members on `Document` that forward to it: `Document.LoadDocx`, `SaveAsDocx`, `ToHtml`,
  `SaveAsMarkdown`. `SaveAsPdf` and `PdfConvert` (namespace `Egap.Documents.Pdf`) write PDF.
- Options are objects with `init` properties, set in an object initializer and passed to the call: `PdfReadOptions`,
  `PdfSaveOptions`, `PdfRenderOptions`, `PdfExportOptions`, `PdfConvertOptions`, `LayoutOptions`, `WorkbookLoadOptions`.
- Damaged input is repaired and reported, not thrown: `pdf.Warnings` (`PdfWarning`), a `Load` overload with
  `out IReadOnlyList<ConversionWarning>`, and the list `Document.Save` returns. A `Strict` option throws instead.
- Sizes are PDF points (1/72 inch). `Length.Mm(15)`, `Length.Cm`, `Length.In` and `Length.Pt` (namespace `Egap.Pdf`) turn
  into points by themselves. Page indexes in code count from 0; `PdfPageRange.Parse("1-3,z")` takes page numbers from 1.
- Images, fonts and drawing come from Egami: a page renders to an Egami `Raster<Rgba8>` (namespaces `Egami` and
  `Egami.Pixels`), and draws onto any Egami.Drawing `Canvas`.
- Egap never opens a network connection by itself: the resolver, base folder or `HttpClient` you pass decides what a
  document may fetch.

## Entry points

- `Document.Load(path | stream)` reads any built-in format, told apart by content; `Document.Identify(path)` gives the
  `DocumentFormatKind` without loading, and `Document.IsEncrypted(path)` says whether it needs a password
  (`DocumentLoadOptions.Password` or `PasswordCallback`).
- `doc.Save(path)` writes by extension and returns the `ConversionWarning`s for what the format could not hold. Format
  classes give options: `DocxFormat`, `RtfFormat.Save`, `OdtFormat.Save`, `TextFormat`, and `doc.SaveAsDocx`, `ToText`.
- `new Document()`, `doc.AddSection().Body.AddParagraph(...)` and `AddTable(rows, columns)` build a tree;
  `new DocumentBuilder(doc)` writes at a cursor (`Write`, `Writeln`, `StartTable`, `InsertCell`, `EndRow`, `EndTable`,
  `InsertImage`, `InsertField`, `InsertTableOfContents`, `Font`, `ParagraphFormat`).
- `doc.Descendants<Paragraph>()`, `node.GetText()`, `doc.Find`, `doc.Replace`, `doc.Sections`, `doc.Styles`,
  `doc.Revisions` (`AcceptAll`, `RejectAll`), `doc.Protection`, `doc.Properties`.
- `doc.SaveAsPdf(path, new PdfExportOptions { Tagged = true, Conformance = ... })` and `doc.ToPdf()`: PDF export.
- `PdfConvert.FromFile`, `FromImages`: one-call conversions to PDF; `PdfToDocument.Convert(pdf)` and `Document.LoadPdf`:
  PDF to a document.
- `doc.Layout(LayoutOptions)` gives a `DocumentLayout`; each page `Render(dpi)`s to a raster or `Draw`s on a canvas.
- `doc.FillMergeFields`, `MailMerge`, `MailMergeAll` with `MergeData.From(...)`; `DocumentCompare.Run(original, revised)`;
  `Report.Create(r => ...)`.

## Samples

Load, edit and save:

```csharp
using Egap.Documents;

Document doc = Document.Load("report.docx");                      // any format Egap reads, told apart by content
foreach (Paragraph p in doc.Descendants<Paragraph>())
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{p.ListLabel?.Text} {p.GetText()}");    // list labels computed as Word numbers them
}

DocumentBuilder builder = new(doc);                               // edit from code at a cursor
builder.Writeln("Added at the end.");
doc.Replace("colour", "color");                                   // also where the text crosses runs
IReadOnlyList<TextMatch> found = doc.Find("color");               // paragraph, offset and text of each match
doc.Save("report-edited.docx");                                   // what the model does not name is kept
IReadOnlyList<ConversionWarning> dropped = doc.Save("report.txt"); // the format from the extension, with what it left out
```

DOCX to tagged PDF:

```csharp
using Egap.Documents;
using Egap.Documents.Pdf;

Document report = Document.Load("report.docx");
report.SaveAsPdf("report.pdf", new PdfExportOptions { Tagged = true });
```

Pages as images:

```csharp
using Egap.Documents;
using Egap.Documents.Layout;

Document doc = Document.Load("report.docx");
DocumentLayout pages = doc.Layout();                              // pages, lines and boxes linked to the model
pages.Pages[0].Render(dpi: 150).Save("page1.png");
```

PDF back to DOCX:

```csharp
using Egap.Documents;
using Egap.Pdf;
using Egap.Documents.Pdf;

using PdfDocument pdf = PdfDocument.Open("paper.pdf");
Document flow = PdfToDocument.Convert(pdf);
flow.Save("paper.docx");
```

Mail merge:

```csharp
using Egap.Documents;

Document letter = Document.Load("letter.docx");
IReadOnlyList<ConversionWarning> missing = letter.FillMergeFields(MergeData.From(new Dictionary<string, object?>
{
    ["Name"] = "Kari Nordmann",
    ["Amount"] = 1234.5m,
    ["Due"] = new DateOnly(2026, 11, 1),
}));
letter.Save("letter-kari.docx");
```

Compare two versions:

```csharp
using Egap.Documents;
using Egap.Documents.Comparing;

Document original = Document.Load("contract-v1.docx");
Document revised = Document.Load("contract-v2.docx");

DocumentComparison comparison = DocumentCompare.Run(original, revised, new DocumentCompareOptions { Author = "Legal" });
Console.WriteLine(comparison);                                       // "12 changes: 40 words inserted, 25 deleted"
comparison.Document.Save("contract-redline.docx");                   // open it in Word to review the changes
```

Encrypted files:

```csharp
using Egap.Documents;

if (Document.IsEncrypted("contract.docx"))
{
    Document contract = Document.Load("contract.docx", new DocumentLoadOptions
    {
        PasswordCallback = attempt => attempt <= 3 ? AskUser($"Password for contract.docx (try {attempt} of 3)") : null,
    });
    contract.SaveAsDocx("contract-copy.docx", new DocxSaveOptions { Password = "new password" });
}

static string? AskUser(string prompt) => null;                    // your program's own password prompt
```

## Common mistakes

- Loading `.html`, `.mht`, `.epub` or `.md` with `Document.Load` without the add-on: it throws a `NotSupportedException`
  that names the package. Add Egap.Documents.Html or Egap.Documents.Markdown and call `HtmlFormat.Register()` or
  `MarkdownFormat.Register()` once at startup.
- Disposing a `Document`: it is not disposable. The `PdfDocument`s that `ToPdf`, `PdfConvert.FromImages` and the
  in-memory `FromFile` overloads return are, so put `using` on those.
- Missing `using Egap.Documents.Pdf;`: `SaveAsPdf`, `ToPdf` and `Document.LoadPdf` are extension members there, so
  without it they do not compile.
- Writing `using Egap.Pdf.Conversion;`. That package is retired; its types are in `Egap.Documents.Pdf` (and the Docling
  types in `Egap.Documents`).
- Ignoring the warnings `Save` returns. Saving to a format that cannot hold something (Markdown, text) drops it and says so.
- Expecting `Save` to choose the format from anything but the extension: an unknown extension throws an
  `ArgumentException`; call the format's class to write another.
- Changing text run by run. `doc.Replace` and `doc.Find` work where text crosses runs; `DocumentBuilder` keeps formatting
  at the cursor.
- Expecting the same PDF on every machine by default. Layout may use system fonts; `LayoutOptions { Fonts =
  FontSettings.Portable }` uses only embedded fonts and the bundled substitutes, and `Strict = true` throws a
  `LayoutException` instead of degrading.
- Tracked changes printed by surprise: PDF export prints them accepted unless `PdfExportOptions.RevisionView` says
  `Markup` or `Original`.
- Untrusted files: DOCX, RTF, ODT, HTML and EPUB are read under `DocumentLimits`; a file past them throws a
  `DocumentLimitException`. Keep the defaults or lower them.
- Spreadsheets are a separate package: `Document.Identify` reports `Xlsx`, but loading a workbook as a document needs
  Egap.Spreadsheets and `SpreadsheetFormat.Register()`.
